title: Sliding Window Maximum
summary: Given an array of integers, a sliding window of size k moves from the start to the end of the array.
statement: Given an array of integers, a sliding window of size k moves from the start to the end of the array. At each step, the window displays the k consecutive elements. The task is to return the maximum value within each window as it slides.
constraints: Return one maximum for each consecutive length-k window, in window order.
hints: A smaller earlier value cannot become a future maximum while a larger later value remains.
Keep candidate indices in a deque with decreasing values, discarding expired indices from the front.
Expire indices outside the window. Remove no-larger values from the back. Append the new index and emit the front once a full window exists.
Each index enters and leaves the deque at most once, giving linear total work.
editorial: Store indices so expiration can be checked precisely. Values along the deque decrease: when a new value arrives, remove smaller or equal values at the back, since the new value is at least as good and expires later. Remove indices before the current window from the front. The front then holds the current maximum. Begin emitting only after k elements have arrived.

tests.explanation: The six windows have maxima 3,3,5,5,6,7. A maximum stops counting when its index leaves the window.
The only window contains the only value 1.
